texts.orig: Q: I’m just starting out as a PM and wondering what makes product managers
texts.text: Q: I’m just starting out as a PM and wondering what makes product managers

texts.label: text
texts.orig: . What habits should I be building early on?
texts.text: . What habits should I be building early on?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: I was a very mediocre PM at first—I wouldn’t have hired me. But I did learn fast, mostly by watching how the best PMs operated. How they ran meetings, how they organized documents, how they made decisions—and then modeling these behaviors and habits.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Don’t get overwhelmed by this list. There’s a lot here, yes, but you don’t need to nail all of these overnight, or ever. My advice to you is to skim through the list, pick one habit you want to work on, and focus on that habit for the next two weeks. If you want more time, stick with it. Otherwise, pick a new habit. Take it easy, but keep at it. For extra credit, start your own list! Watch the best PMs around you and jot down what they’re doing well. If you note any other essential habits for new, highly effective PMs to develop, leave a comment 👇

texts.orig: 3. Great PMs hold the bar high for the work they, and their teammates, do
texts.text: 3. Great PMs hold the bar high for the work they, and their teammates, do

texts.label: text
texts.orig: They resist the urge to let people settle for good enough. They push their team, and themselves, to make documents clearer, to make meetings more valuable, and to help people do the best work of their lives.
texts.text: They resist the urge to let people settle for good enough. They push their team, and themselves, to make documents clearer, to make meetings more valuable, and to help people do the best work of their lives.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Some ways to build this habit:
texts.text: Some ways to build this habit:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: When you see subpar performance, don’t ignore it. Push back, e.g. “Hey, this strategy doc is confusing, tbh—what if you tweak X, Y, and Z to clarify your point?”
texts.text: When you see subpar performance, don’t ignore it. Push back, e.g. “Hey, this strategy doc is confusing, tbh—what if you tweak X, Y, and Z to clarify your point?”

texts.label: text
texts.orig: When you’re about to share a PRD/one-pager, ask yourself: What’s

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Make sure to review each major document, meeting, and presentation that your team is outputting—make sure the work your team puts out into the org is always A+.
texts.text: Make sure to review each major document, meeting, and presentation that your team is outputting—make sure the work your team puts out into the org is always A+.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 4. Great PMs hunt for misalignment and quickly push everyone back into alignment
texts.text: 4. Great PMs hunt for misalignment and quickly push everyone back into alignment

texts.label: text
texts.orig: They know that team dysfunction is often rooted in people simply having different information, motives, or priorities. They know that rooting these out is some of the highest-leverage work they can ever do.
texts.text: They know that team dysfunction is often rooted in people simply having different information, motives, or priorities. They know that rooting these out is some of the highest-leverage work they can ever do.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Some ways to build this habit:
texts.text: Some ways to build this habit:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: When reviewing new designs, always bring people back to “What problem are we trying to solve here?”
texts.text: When reviewing new designs, always bring people back to “What problem are we trying to solve here?”

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: When you get a hint that team members are misaligned (e.g. quoting data not everyone has seen, optimizing for different goals, shifting priorities), just say, “We may be misaligned on this. What’s your understanding of X?”
texts.text: When you get a hint that team members are misaligned (e.g. quoting data not everyone has seen, optimizing for different goals, shifting priorities), just say, “We may be misaligned on this. What’s your understanding of X?”

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Create, and keep coming back to, a source-of-truth document that crystallizes the goal, the succinct problem being solved, key assumptions, and key decisions.
texts.text: Create, and keep coming back to, a source-of-truth document that crystallizes the goal, the succinct problem being solved, key assumptions, and key decisions.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 5. Great PMs always have a point of view, but loosely held
texts.text: 5. Great PMs always have a point of view, but loosely held

texts.label: text
texts.orig: They know they aren’t on the team simply to coordinate other people’s work—that their team is looking to them for new ideas, novel insights, and to push their thinking. They also know they need to be ready to quickly change their POV when they have new information.
texts.text: They know they aren’t on the team simply to coordinate other people’s work—that their team is looking to them for new ideas, novel insights, and to push their thinking. They also know they need to be ready to quickly change their POV when they have new information.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Some ways to build this habit:
texts.text: Some ways to build this habit:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Keep this question in your mind: If someone were to ask for my opinion right now, what would I say?
texts.text: Keep this question in your mind: If someone were to ask for my opinion right now, what would I say?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: When you don’t have a strong POV (e.g. which design to go with, whether to launch the experiment or not), create a simple pros and cons list.
texts.text: When you don’t have a strong POV (e.g. which design to go with, whether to launch the experiment or not), create a simple pros and cons list.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: When you change your point of view based on new information, share it publicly. Make it very clear you aren’t stuck in your views.
texts.text: When you change your point of view based on new information, share it publicly. Make it very clear you aren’t stuck in your views.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 7. Great PMs endlessly look for blockers to unblock
texts.text: 7. Great PMs endlessly look for blockers to unblock

texts.label: text
texts.orig: They’re always on the hunt for bottlenecks, unmade decisions, and anything that is keeping their team from operating like a well-oiled machine.
texts.text: They’re always on the hunt for bottlenecks, unmade decisions, and anything that is keeping their team from operating like a well-oiled machine.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Some ways to build this habit:
texts.text: Some ways to build this habit:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Always prioritize tasks that unblock your team members.
texts.text: Always prioritize tasks that unblock your team members.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Ask your team members often: What’s slowing you down?
texts.text: Ask your team members often: What’s slowing you down?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Look around corners—what’s a looming soon-to-be blocker that you can keep from becoming a blocker?
texts.text: Look around corners—what’s a looming soon-to-be blocker that you can keep from becoming a blocker?

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 8. Great PMs build a tight leadership triad with their EM and DM
texts.text: 8. Great PMs build a tight leadership triad with their EM and DM

texts.label: text
texts.orig: They know that their team operates best when the leaders of the team speak with one voice, and since most of the team reports to the eng. manager and the design manager, it’s essential that these three leaders work as an aligned unit.
texts.text: They know that their team operates best when the leaders of the team speak with one voice, and since most of the team reports to the eng. manager and the design manager, it’s essential that these three leaders work as an aligned unit.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Some ways to build this habit:
texts.text: Some ways to build this habit:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Sit next to your EM and DM (when possible).
texts.text: Sit next to your EM and DM (when possible).

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Have a weekly meeting to align on priorities, share information, and unblock the team.
texts.text: Have a weekly meeting to align on priorities, share information, and unblock the team.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Spend time outside of work hours in order to connect as humans.
texts.text: Spend time outside of work hours in order to connect as humans.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 9. Great PMs frequently remind teammates of how their work connects to the mission
texts.text: 9. Great PMs frequently remind teammates of how their work connects to the mission

texts.label: text
texts.orig: They know that people don’t work at companies to pull levers, move metrics, or hit goals.
texts.text: They know that people don’t work at companies to pull levers, move metrics, or hit goals.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Some ways to build this habit:
texts.text: Some ways to build this habit:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Include your team’s mission and/or vision in every strategy document.
texts.text: Include your team’s mission and/or vision in every strategy document.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: In kickoff meetings, find opportunities to remind the team how this random project enables the team/company to come closer to its mission.
texts.text: In kickoff meetings, find opportunities to remind the team how this random project enables the team/company to come closer to its mission.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: At the top of your roadmap documents, include your team vision or mission.
texts.text: At the top of your roadmap documents, include your team vision or mission.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 10. Great PMs speak with their customers regularly
texts.text: 10. Great PMs speak with their customers regularly

texts.label: text
texts.orig: They know that no matter how confident they are about what their customers want, they are frequently wrong.
texts.text: They know that no matter how confident they are about what their customers want, they are frequently wrong.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Some ways to build this habit:
texts.text: Some ways to build this habit:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Create systems where you and your team interact with customers regularly, like a weekly “Lunch with a customer,” a monthly CX rotation, or a quarterly customer visit.
texts.text: Create systems where you and your team interact with customers regularly, like a weekly “Lunch with a customer,” a monthly CX rotation, or a quarterly customer visit.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Make an agreement that for any feature that takes more than X weeks to design and build, you first talk to five potential users/customers to validate the desirability of the feature.
texts.text: Make an agreement that for any feature that takes more than X weeks to design and build, you first talk to five potential users/customers to validate the desirability of the feature.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Build a one-on-one relationship with some of your larger customers, and use that connection to learn about their pain points, gather ideas, and get quick and raw feedback.
texts.text: Build a one-on-one relationship with some of your larger customers, and use that connection to learn about their pain points, gather ideas, and get quick and raw feedback.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 11. Great PMs anticipate what’s around the corner so that they can get ahead of it
texts.text: 11. Great PMs anticipate what’s around the corner so that they can get ahead of it

texts.label: text
texts.orig: They know that the most successful PMs are the most prepared PMs, and the best way to be prepared is to have more time to prepare.
texts.text: They know that the most successful PMs are the most prepared PMs, and the best way to be prepared is to have more time to prepare.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Some ways to build this habit:
texts.text: Some ways to build this habit:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Schedule a 30-minute meeting with yourself, each Monday morning or Friday afternoon, to look at your upcoming week and note meetings and deliverables you need to get ahead of.
texts.text: Schedule a 30-minute meeting with yourself, each Monday morning or Friday afternoon, to look at your upcoming week and note meetings and deliverables you need to get ahead of.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: When you hear of priority or strategy changes happening up the ladder, ask yourself: How could this impact our team, and what could we start prepping now?
texts.text: When you hear of priority or strategy changes happening up the ladder, ask yourself: How could this impact our team, and what could we start prepping now?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: When everything is going smoothly, ask yourself: How could I help my team move even faster?
texts.text: When everything is going smoothly, ask yourself: How could I help my team move even faster?

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 12. Great PMs make sure everyone has a chance to be heard
texts.text: 12. Great PMs make sure everyone has a chance to be heard

texts.label: text
texts.orig: They know that most of the best ideas won’t come from them, and that the simple act of listening goes a very long way.
texts.text: They know that most of the best ideas won’t come from them, and that the simple act of listening goes a very long way.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Some ways to build this habit:
texts.text: Some ways to build this habit:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: At the end of meetings, check in with people who’ve been quiet to see if they have anything to add.
texts.text: At the end of meetings, check in with people who’ve been quiet to see if they have anything to add.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Before finalizing your strategy, roadmap, or spec, give your team a chance to give feedback asynchronously.
texts.text: Before finalizing your strategy, roadmap, or spec, give your team a chance to give feedback asynchronously.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Organize brainstorms and offer types of ideation sessions where team members can contribute their ideas.
texts.text: Organize brainstorms and offer types of ideation sessions where team members can contribute their ideas.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 13. Great PMs amplify the successes and contributions of team members
texts.text: 13. Great PMs amplify the successes and contributions of team members

texts.label: text
texts.orig: They know that the success of a PM is measured primarily by the success of their team.
texts.text: They know that the success of a PM is measured primarily by the success of their team.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Some ways to build this habit:
texts.text: Some ways to build this habit:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Forward examples of great work to your teammates’ managers.
texts.text: Forward examples of great work to your teammates’ managers.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Highlight team members’ achievements in your team meetings and email updates.
texts.text: Highlight team members’ achievements in your team meetings and email updates.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Start a “#team-huzzah”-type Slack channel to celebrate wins, big and small.
texts.text: Start a “#team-huzzah”-type Slack channel to celebrate wins, big and small.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 14. Great PMs bring good vibes to the team
texts.text: 14. Great PMs bring good vibes to the team

texts.label: text
texts.orig: They know that they are the unofficial-but-de-facto leader of the team, and that the vibes they bring trickle down throughout the team.
texts.text: They know that they are the unofficial-but-de-facto leader of the team, and that the vibes they bring trickle down throughout the team.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Some ways to build this habit:
texts.text: Some ways to build this habit:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Always start off each meeting with energy and positivity.
texts.text: Always start off each meeting with energy and positivity.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Find something fun for the team to do regularly—a weekly happy hour, a monthly team-building event.
texts.text: Find something fun for the team to do regularly—a weekly happy hour, a monthly team-building event.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Bring surprise and delight to regular events—a team band at your all-hands, goats on your Zoom calls, birthday surprises at your standup.
